newsitem.title: UK: Britain finds more money to help "rough sleepers".
newsitem.headline: Britain finds more money to help "rough sleepers".

text.p: The British government announced a 27-million-pound ($44 million) programme on Thursday to help people sleeping rough in London to find shelter and to extend its "Rough Sleepers Initiative" to other cities.
The government claims the initiative has reduced the number of people sleeping rough on any one night in central London to less than 300 from over 1,000 in 1990 when the scheme began.
The sight of people sleeping in the street, notably in the theatre area close to Trafalgar Square, is often cited by tourists as one of the more unpleasant aspects of the capital.
The money will go towards resettlement, usually in hostels as a first step, with central government working alongside local authorities, voluntary organisations and charities.
It includes two million pounds ($3.25 million) specifically for people with mental health problems who sleep rough.

Surveys show that up to 40 percent of people sleeping rough do not want a bed in a hostel, usually because of the unsocial behaviour of other residents puts them off, but Housing Minister David Curry said no one would be forced into a hostel.
"Hosing people down and rounding them up is not part of this programme," he told a news conference.
